title: The ML Workflow 🔄
description: Walk through the end‑to‑end process: data, training, evaluation, deployment — like a chef perfecting a recipe.

slides.title: From Idea to Intelligent App 🚀
slides.content:
# The ML Pipeline

Every ML project follows a similar lifecycle:
1. **Data Collection** – gather relevant data.
2. **Data Preparation** – clean and format the data.
3. **Model Training** – teach the algorithm.
4. **Model Evaluation** – test how well it learned.
5. **Deployment** – put it into production.
6. **Monitoring & Iteration** – keep improving.

Think of it as a chef: source ingredients, prep, cook, taste, serve, and tweak the recipe.

slides.title: 1. Data Collection & 2. Preparation 📋
slides.content:
# Getting the Right Ingredients

- **Collection**: Gather data from databases, APIs, sensors, or web scraping.
- **Preparation**: Clean missing values, remove outliers, convert formats, and split into **training** and **test** sets.

💡 *Garbage in = garbage out.* If the data is messy, the model will be too.

quizData.question: Why do we split data into training and test sets?

options.text: To make the computer run faster
To evaluate the model on unseen data and check for overfitting
Because the algorithm requires exactly two files
To double the amount of data

quizData.explanation: A test set simulates how the model will perform on new, unseen examples, preventing over‑confidence.

slides.title: 3. Model Training 🏋️
slides.content:
# Learning from Examples

During training, the algorithm looks at the training data and tries to find the best mathematical function that maps inputs to outputs.

- For regression: find the line/curve that best fits the points.
- For classification: find the boundary that separates classes.

It adjusts internal **parameters** (like knobs) to minimise errors. This is where the magic happens!

slides.title: 4. Evaluation & 5. Deployment 📊
slides.content:
# How Good is Your Chef?

- **Evaluation**: Use the test set to measure performance (accuracy, precision, etc.). If it’s not good enough, go back and tweak.
- **Deployment**: Integrate the model into an app, website, or device so real users can benefit.

A model that works in a notebook is useless unless it can serve predictions in the real world.

quizData.question: What typically happens after a model fails to meet performance goals during evaluation?

options.text: Go back and improve data, features, or try a different algorithm
Delete the project and start a new career

quizData.explanation: ML is iterative! Poor evaluation results mean you revisit earlier steps — better data, feature engineering, or model selection.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## The Real World is Messy
Deployment isn’t the end. Models need monitoring because data can change over time (concept drift). A model that was great last year might be terrible today.
